statement: In a finite undirected graph, if v lies on every o-to-A path and every a_star-to-b path for some a_star in nonempty A, then {o connects to A,a_star connects to b} is contained in {o connects to b,o connects to A}; product percolation consequently satisfies P(o connects to b)>=P(o connects to A)min_a P(a connects to b).
assumptions: The two separator hypotheses hold for deterministic G,v,a_star
Independent Bernoulli edge states with arbitrary probabilities in [0,1] only for the probabilistic product conclusion
source: owner-own-work: campaign derivation w426, 2026-10-10; route context Kozma-Nitzan arXiv:2401.12397v1 Conjectures 1-2
proof_or_counterexample: On the intersected event, a chosen open o-to-A path supplies an open o-to-v segment, and an open a_star-to-b path supplies an open v-to-b segment. Concatenate to connect o to b. Harris positive association bounds the intersection probability below by the product of the two increasing-event probabilities.
remaining_gap: No deterministic witness guaranteed on arbitrary cyclic graphs; independent audit pending.

statement: The Kozma-Nitzan product gluing inequality holds for every finite forest, every nonempty relay set A, and arbitrary independent edge probabilities in [0,1]; its multiplicative coefficient 1 is optimal.
proof_or_counterexample: If A has a vertex outside b's graph component, the minimum connection probability is zero; if o and b are in different graph components then either this happens or P(o connects to A)=0. Otherwise all relevant vertices lie in one tree. Project each relay to the unique o-b path and choose the projection nearest o, denoted v, and a relay a_star attaining it. Every o-to-A path contains v and every a_star-to-b path contains v. Apply L1. A three-vertex path o-a-b with A={a} attains equality for any positive edge probabilities, proving sharpness.
remaining_gap: Tree projection has no direct replacement in cyclic finite lattice windows; independent audit pending.

statement: Selecting the first reached relay in an arbitrary fixed order need not preserve its unconditional probability of reaching b; even the averaged first-relay inequality can fail under independent percolation.
proof_or_counterexample: P(I=a1)=rs, P(I=a2)=r(1-s), and P(a1 connects to b)=t, P(a2 connects to b)=st. Conditioning on I=a2 forces the middle edge closed, so its conditional terminal probability is 0. P(o connects to b)=rst, but the averaged unconditional relay sum is rst(2-s), larger by rst(1-s)>0. At r=s=t=1/2 the true probability is 1/8 and the sum 3/16.
remaining_gap: Only the arbitrary-order auxiliary bridge is refuted. Nondecreasing marginal order and uniform near-one gluing remain separate assertions.

statement: For every epsilon in (0,1), delta_star=1-sqrt(1-epsilon) is the largest delta in (0,1] for which near-one gluing holds uniformly on all finite forests. It is a necessary upper bound on any admissible modulus for all finite graphs.
assumptions: Independent Bernoulli bond states with arbitrary edge probabilities in [0,1]
Strict premises and conclusion as in Kozma-Nitzan Conjecture 3
proof_or_counterexample: L2 gives terminal probability > (1-delta_star)^2=1-epsilon. For any larger delta choose a two-edge path o-a-b with both probabilities x strictly between max(0,1-delta) and sqrt(1-epsilon); the premises hold but x^2<1-epsilon.
remaining_gap: This sharp modulus is sufficient only in the forest subfamily; arbitrary cyclic graph sufficiency is not proved.

statement: In arbitrary finite graphs there need not exist a fixed relay a_star such that {o connects to A,a_star connects to b} is contained in {o connects to b}; this bridge fails on a square with a pendant terminal.
assumptions: All independent edge probabilities strictly between 0 and 1 to obtain positive-probability failures
proof_or_counterexample: For a_star=a1 open exactly o-a2,a1-v,v-b; for a_star=a2 interchange the relay names. Each selection violates the claimed event inclusion. At half weights product gluing remains valid: 7/32-(3/4)(9/32)=1/128.
remaining_gap: Only a deterministic witness bridge is refuted; stochastic gluing and C0023 are not refuted.

statement: For each integer 3<=d<=10, theta_d(p_c(d))=0 for independent nearest-neighbor Bernoulli BOND percolation on Z^d, with theta_d(p)=P_p(|C(0)|=infinity) and p_c(d)=inf{p in [0,1]:theta_d(p)>0}.
assumptions: Undirected edges between lattice vertices at l1 distance 1
source: Kozma-Nitzan arXiv:2401.12397v1, Section 2.1 and Theorem 6; exact intake C0023 problems.jsonl line 23
